questions: What happens when A_i becomes 0 after subtraction - does the index i remain in set S or get removed?
Is the condition "If S=" checking if set S is empty or if S equals something else?
When does the game actually end - immediately when S becomes empty, or after a player's turn when no valid moves remain?
Can a player choose an index i where A_i = 0, or must A_i be strictly greater than 0?
What is the exact winning condition - does a player win by making the last valid move, or by causing S to become empty?
If multiple indices have the same value, how does optimal play determine which index to choose?
Does the constraint "1≤A_i" apply at the start of each turn or only when choosing an index to modify?
What happens if all A_i values become 0 but set S is not empty - can players still make moves?
answers: Once index i is added to S it stays there; there's no removal rule even if A_i later becomes 0.
'S=' should read 'S = {1,2,...,N}' -- the condition triggers once all indices have been added to S, not when S is empty.
The game ends immediately once S becomes {1,2,...,N} (not empty), right after the operation that completes it.
A player may choose i only if 1 ≤ A_i, as stated.
The winning condition is performing the operation that makes S = {1,2,...,N}; that player wins immediately.
Not applicable; a player may choose any valid index freely, no tie-breaking is specified or needed.
The condition 1 ≤ A_i applies at the moment of choosing an index to modify.
This can't happen before the game ends, since the problem guarantees a valid move exists until the game concludes.
inline_prompts: Fennec and Snuke are playing a board game. You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of positive integers of length N. Also, there is a set S, which is initially empty. Fennec and Snuke take turns performing the following operation in order, starting with Fennec. - Choose an index i such that 1\leq A_i. Subtract 1 from A_i, and if i\notin S, add i to S. Once index i is added to S it stays there; there's no removal rule even if A_i later becomes 0. - If S=, the game ends and the player who performed the last operation wins. Note that it can be proven that until a winner is determined and the game ends, players can always make a move (there exists some i such that 1\leq A_i). Both Fennec and Snuke play optimally to win. Determine who will win. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print Fennec if Fennec wins, or Snuke if Snuke wins. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Fennec, outputs such as fennec, FENNEC, or fEnNeC will also be accepted. Constraints - 1\leq N\leq 2\times 10^5 - 1\leq A_i\leq 10^9 (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
